text:
rachel: Quick note from pairing with a new dev — found a cluster of README/codeblock drift across our sample-apps. Things I saw: mismatched env var names, curl examples missing Content-Type, two different JS import styles, and an embeddings example that passes `dim` instead of `dimension` which causes the SDK to raise a validation error. New hires keep copy/pasting and getting confusing errors.

omar: Oof. Which files?

rachel: `examples/notes/README.md`, `docs/embeddings.md`, and `quickstarts/node/README.md`. Snippets pulled from different eras. Example that tripped the new dev: embedding call in docs uses wrong param name:
```js
// bad (old/typo)
const resp = await client.createEmbedding({ model: 'embed-small', dim: 1536, input: ['a', 'b'] });
// SDK expects `dimension` not `dim` -> fails validation
```

kevin: Good catch. We changed the param name when we bumped the embeddings API in v0.9. New users copy the docs and run into a cryptic schema error.

rachel: Also saw two Node quickstart variants: one uses `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` + `new Redwood.Client(...)` (broken for our current exports), and another uses `import { Client } from '@redwood/inference'`. The curl examples also had `X-Api-Key` in one spot and `Authorization: Bearer` in another.

omar: Can you paste the problematic curl?

rachel: Sure:
```bash
# bad
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"input":["hello"]}'
# good
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":["hello"], "dimension":1536}'
```

kevin: We should also avoid hardcoded `sk-` literals in examples. I grep'd the repo and found a couple of stray tokens in archived READMEs.

rachel: Proposed fixes I'll include in a tiny docs PR:
- Update embeddings docs to use `dimension` and include a quick note about model vector sizes.
- Standardize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY across all quickstarts.
- Replace any `X-Api-Key` or `Token:` headers with `Authorization: Bearer`.
- Fix JS import to use named `Client` and add a short note on Node versions for top-level await.
- Add a single-line gotchas box: "Avoid hardcoded tokens, create client once, include Content-Type in curl".

omar: Can you also add a one-liner about not re-instantiating the client inside loops? We've had users trigger connection storms recreating clients per request.

rachel: Yep. I'll show the pattern in both JS and Python: create client once, then retry requests.

kevin: Can we add an automated docs check to catch `dim:` and `X-Api-Key`, and literal `sk-` strings inside triple-backtick codeblocks? A grep-based CI job would be quick to add.

ci-bot: I can add a docs CI step that fails on matches for regexes: `\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`, `X-Api-Key`, `\bdim:\s*\d+\b` in code fences.

docs-bot: Reminder: small docs-only PRs should include a changelog entry and reference an issue.

rachel: Filed issue #4999 to track snippet parity + CI checks. I'll open PR titled "docs: unify quickstart snippets & fix embeddings param" and tag @omar and @kevin for review.

omar: Thanks — these are low-friction but will save a lot of time for new users. :seedling:

kevin: After the PR lands, can we run the newbie onboarding checklist with a fresh account to verify nothing else trips people up? Happy to help test.
